chunk_findings.detail: The new guard fails open when tree comparison is impossible. In `reviewed_other_tree`, `if not was or not now or was == now: return ""` means a review record with no `tree_sha`/`source_tree`, or an item whose current worktree is missing/unreadable (`now == ""`), produces no stale message. `review_settle.py` only blocks the refute-all pass path when `stale` is non-empty, so such a state still allows a failed/unavailable gate to be upgraded to passed. Example: a gate record whose evidence contains the review log and one finding but no `tree_sha`/`source_tree` is triaged `--refuted`; `was` is falsy, `reviewed_other_tree` returns `""`, and `review_settle` proceeds to pass without the passed gate naming any reviewed head. This violates the B835d22b138 requirement for a pass to name the head it reviewed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:reviewed_other_tree

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert gate.evidence.get("tree_sha"), "a passed must name the tree it reviewed"` only checks that `evidence` contains a non-empty `tree_sha`; it never compares that SHA with the tree/HEAD the repository holds now. The original bug was exactly that a passed gate retained the old round’s evidence, which already had a non-empty old `tree_sha`. For example, `gate.evidence = {"tree_sha": "<old_reviewed_head>"}` satisfies this assertion even though the pass does not name the current head, so this test does not enforce the stated invariant.

<result>Soft upgrades look feasible, and I've added the phase and tasks, but nothing is implemented. I made no source edits. I recorded the operator's words with `session prompt` and settled no decision, so the architecture below is a recommendation for the operator.

## Findings

| Question | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| What the server is today (`R-soft-startup-state`) | CONFIRMED | A hand-rolled stdlib stdio JSON-RPC server (`ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py`). It imports the whole library: 158 of 628 modules before any call, plus 44 function-local imports. It holds about 300 MB RSS. |
| Startup cost | CONFIRMED | `initialize` takes 6.3–6.5 s over stdio, and 20.9 s under cProfile. The time is in the instructions build, which folds the whole event log about 6 times. `tools/list` is about 10 ms for 123 tools / 108 KB. |
| State the process holds | CONFIRMED | Per connection only: protocol, client info, agent, called_from and notice counters. The existing `[mcp].on_upgrade=reexec` already hands this state across an exec. |
| After the files change | CONFIRMED | The running process keeps its old code and refuses writes through the skew guard. `reexec` and `notify` already exist, but `listChanged` is false everywhere. |
| In-process reload (B) (`R-soft-inprocess-reload`) | REFUTED | Lazy imports would mix old and new modules, so B is unsafe. |
| Does Claude Code honour `list_changed`? (`R-soft-claude-listchanged`) | CONFIRMED | Claude Code 2.1.296 re-fetched `tools/list`, including on an unsolicited notification sent while idle. A tool added mid-session became callable, ToolSearch found it, and a removed tool became uncallable. |
| Does a changed schema reach the model? | Unreliable | The client re-fetched, but the model kept calling a tool with the old argument name, with ToolSearch on or off. Each variant was run once, with haiku. |
| Do prompt changes refresh? | Not shown | No `prompts/list` re-fetch followed the notification in `-p` mode. That may be an artifact of print mode. |
| Does a shim work end to end? (`R-soft-shim-prototype`) | CONFIRMED | A 28-line stdlib shim hot-swapped its worker under a live Claude Code session. The worker pid changed, a new tool appeared, and the connection stayed up. The prototype has no drain, no id-collision handling and no crash handling. |
| Other clients and the 2026-07-28 revision (`R-soft-client-table`) | THEORETICAL | Cursor is reported to ignore `list_changed` (forum thread 161459). A May-2026 report says Claude Code did too, which my 2.1.296 probe contradicts. 2026-07-28 moves `list_changed` to an opt-in `subscriptions/listen` stream and adds `ttlMs` caching. ddflow implements no `subscriptions/listen` and sets `tools/list` `ttlMs` to 1 hour, so a 2026-07-28 client could keep a stale list for an hour. Codex, Gemini, VS Code, opencode, Kimi and Qwen are untested. |

Sources: the MCP tools page (2025-06-18), the 2026-07-28 changelog, and the Cursor forum thread. The probe servers are in the scratchpad `lc/` directory.

## Recommended architecture

Use A+D together: a stdlib-only shim that owns the stdio connection and the negotiation, and a restartable worker that holds ddflow. The shim serves `initialize` and `tools/list` from a cached snapshot, so startup drops from about 6 s to about 20 ms. When the worker's interface digest changes, the shim re-announces it with `list_changed`, or `subscriptions/listen` on 2026-07-28. Keep `reexec` as the fallback for hard upgrades.

Option C alone avoids a client reconnect but cannot re-announce. Option B is rejected.

## Soft vs hard

The interface digest is a sha256 over the canonical JSON of:
- tool names, schemas, descriptions and annotations
- prompts
- the instructions template
- capabilities
- protocol versions

- **Soft:** the shim and the shim-to-worker protocol are unchanged, and either the digest is unchanged or it changed and all of these hold:
  - the connected client is known to honour `list_changed`
  - the change is additive, a removal, or schema-compatible
  - the worker accepts the previous schema's arguments for one version, because changed schemas don't reliably reach the model
- **Hard:** the shim or the protocol major changed, the client ignores or is unknown for `list_changed`, or an existing tool's required arguments changed incompatibly.

User messages are `soft upgrade applied, no restart needed (N tools added, M removed: announced to <client>)` or `hard upgrade: restart your agent` plus the reason. They go through `ddflow upgrade`, `doctor`, the MCP footer and the SessionStart hook.

chunk_findings.detail: Given a gate whose recorded outcome is `"unavailable"`, when all findings are refuted and `reviewed_other_tree` returns a stale message, this new branch returns text ending in `"{gate} stays failed: {stale}"`. The gate is not failed, only unavailable, so the command response misreports the gate state. The parallel guard in `_settle_after_cap` correctly interpolates `rec.outcome`; this one hardcodes `"failed"` and should do the same.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review_settle.py:43

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds for the `now == ""` branch. The guard `if not was or not now or was == now: return ""` treats an unreadable/absent current source tree as “same tree” and returns no stale message; `review_settle.py` only blocks the triage-to-passed path when `stale` is non-empty. So if a critic gate has evidence with a recorded `tree_sha` but `GE.source_tree(repo)` returns `""` (e.g. the worktree is missing or source-tree computation fails), triaging the two refuted findings still records `passed_on_refutation` over a tree no reviewer has confirmed. The added test `test_a_round_that_names_no_tree_cannot_be_passed_by_triage` monkeypatches only `RV.GE.recorded_content` to `""`; it never simulates `GE.source_tree` returning `""`, so it does not exercise this fail-open case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:reviewed_other_tree

chunk_findings.detail: The new fallback maps a `<head>+clean` fingerprint to that commit's *tree* via `GE.commit_source_tree(wt, base)`, then only compares that tree with `GE.source_tree(wt)`. It never verifies that the current HEAD is still the `base` head named by the evidence. Given a failed/unavailable gate with evidence `tree_sha="A+clean"` and no `source_tree`, where the final HEAD is a different commit B whose tree object is identical to A's tree (e.g. an amended/rebased commit with the same file content but a different parent/message), `was == now`, so `reviewed_other_tree` returns `""`. Triage then may upgrade the gate to passed even though no reviewer saw the final head, which is exactly the B835d22b138 bypass this change is meant to prevent.

**Matrix.** "Cache" is how the client holds the tool list; "Revision" is the MCP protocol revision it offered in `initialize`.

| Client | list_changed (tools) | Cache / reconnect | Transport | Revision | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

No project named "grokbot" turned up. Grok Build and superagent grok-cli are the nearest.

**Findings that change the design:**
- Prompt change notices are not reliable across clients, so no soft upgrade should depend on them.
- Honouring a notification is not the same as the model adopting the change. Only additions and removals are safe to announce.
- Codex, Goose and opencode can already negotiate 2026-07-28. ddflow's fixed one-hour `ttlMs` on `tools/list` will bite those clients.

**Recommended rule.** An upgrade is soft if any of these holds:
- the interface digest is unchanged;
- the change is only additions or removals and the client is known to honour `list_changed`, from the table or because the shim saw it re-fetch `tools/list` after announcing;
- facade mode is on.

Otherwise it is hard, with the reason naming the client. A schema change to an existing tool is soft only with the worker accepting the previous schema for one version, and only for an honouring client. An unknown client is treated as hard, but the first upgrade teaches ddflow (the re-fetch is recorded as `observed`).

Degraded modes for clients that ignore or cache the list:
- **Facade (`ddflow_search` / `ddflow_call`):** makes the swap soft for every client, at a cost in model accuracy.
- **Restart notice:** a line in tool results saying the hard upgrade is pending.
- **Version digest in tool descriptions:** rejected, since a caching client never re-reads descriptions.

**Queue changes:**
- `SU-client-matrix` added under `P-soft-upgrade`. `SU-client-table` now needs `SU-digest` and `SU-client-matrix`.
- Bodies extended on `SU-client-table`, `SU-announce`, `SU-upgrade-integration`, `SU-decision`, `SU-digest` and `SU-e2e-test`.
- New tasks `SU-facade-mode` (needs `MTD-search-call`), `SU-restart-notice` and `SU-client-probe-ci`. The last should share a harness with the existing `RM-client-probes`. `SU-upgrade-integration` now needs the two new ones as well.
- Research notes: Kilo (CONFIRMED), source-read clients (THEORETICAL), closed or doc-only clients (THEORETICAL).
- Bugs filed: `B-research-extends-drops-id`, `B-claim-research-inherits-phase-deps`, `B-update-needs-replaces-silently`, `B-session-prompt-cli-needs-session-id`, and the kind bug above.
- `research add --extends` ignored the ids I gave it and appended all three notes to `R-soft-client-table`. That note's verdict therefore stays THEORETICAL even though the Kilo probe is CONFIRMED.

The post-merge check on main reported `ruff format --check` failed. I changed only a markdown file and did not investigate. My own event log is committed on main; no push.

## Q1: can the server learn that the client handles list_changed?

- **Legacy `initialize` (2025-11-25 and earlier):** there is no negotiated signal (DOCS, spec). Capabilities don't separate honouring clients from ignoring ones. Qwen (ignores) and Gemini (honours) both send `roots.listChanged`. Cline (honours) and Roo (ignores) both send `{}`.
- **2026-07-28:** a `subscriptions/listen` with `toolsListChanged: true` is an explicit opt-in. The server must not send unrequested notification types (DOCS, spec). This is the only reliable signal, and no installed client uses it yet. Claude Code only probes `server/discover` and falls back to 2025-11-25.
- **What the installed clients send at `initialize` (VERIFIED):** Claude Code sends `claude-code` 2.1.296 with `roots.listChanged` and `elicitation`. Kilo sends `kilo` 7.8.12 with `roots: {}`.
- **`clientInfo.version` can't be relied on (SOURCE):** opencode sends `unknown`, Qwen a constant `0.0.1`, Continue a constant `1.0.0`. Those clients can only be keyed by name.
- **Handshake probe:** do not use it as a gate. A `list_changed` sent 0.3 s after `initialized` on Claude Code's respawned connection produced no `tools/list`, though that client honours it on a first connection (VERIFIED, one run, cause UNKNOWN).
- **Recommended:** identify by name against the table, use the listen opt-in where present, and otherwise observe. One re-fetch within 10 s records the client as honouring. It records "ignores" only after two silent notifications in different sessions.

## Q2: can a server make the client disconnect, reload and reconnect?

- **Server-initiated reconnect:** no client does it. I found no reaction to a notification, exit code, SIGHUP or socket across 13 clients (SOURCE, negative greps).
- **Config watchers:** Cline, Roo, Zed, VS Code, Qwen and opencode restart a server on a config change, but only if that server's entry differs. That means rewriting each client's own config file, so I don't recommend it.
- **Claude Code `-p` and stdio exit (VERIFIED):** it respawns the server lazily on the next tool call and re-runs `initialize`. It does not re-fetch `tools/list`. The model kept the old tool list and never saw the new generation's tool. An in-flight call got `Connection closed`. The docs say stdio is not reconnected, so they are wrong for `-p`.
- **Claude Code and an HTTP 404 on the session (VERIFIED):** it re-initializes and retries the same call in about 40 ms. The model sees no error and the tool list is not re-fetched.
- **Kilo (VERIFIED, one run):** it marks the server failed and drops its tools; the `execute` facade vanished in the same run. It does not respawn. Recovery needs a manual connect.
- **Other clients (SOURCE):**
  - Respawn on the next call: VS Code, OpenHands.
  - Respawn via a health monitor: Qwen. Whether a stdio exit reaches it is UNKNOWN.
  - Failed or stale until a manual command: opencode, Gemini, Codex, Cline, Roo, Continue, Goose, Zed.
- **Tool list after respawn:** only VS Code and Qwen re-list tools. Claude Code, OpenHands and Kimi keep the stale list.
- **In-flight calls:** every client read returns an error to the model. Qwen replays idempotent calls, and several retry once on a 404.
- **Verdict:** reconnect is weaker than list_changed. It drops the in-flight call, repays ddflow's 6 to 20 s startup, and mostly leaves the tool list stale. A stable shim never drops the connection. It is a fallback tier only.

## Refined soft/hard rule

1. **Soft, silent:** the digest is unchanged, or the facade is on.
2. **Soft, announced:** the change is additive, a removal, or a compatible schema change, and the client honours list_changed (table, listen opt-in, or observed).
3. **Soft, features pending:** the change is additive or a removal and the client ignores list_changed or is unknown. Old tools keep working and removed tools are served for one more version. The report says new tools appear after a restart. Unknown clients are still announced and observed.
4. **Soft via reconnect:** only for clients marked respawn-and-relist. The report says one in-flight call may fail.
5. **Hard:** a tool or prompt the client already holds changes incompatibly, the client doesn't honour list_changed or doesn't adopt schema changes, and there is no facade or grace. Also hard if the shim or its protocol changed.

This is the operator's split, with two additions. A changed schema of an existing tool is hard even for honouring clients unless the worker grace covers it, because Claude Code re-fetches but does not adopt it (VERIFIED earlier). An additive change is soft for every client.

# Report: managing engineering requirements and standards in ddflow

## What was done
- I wrote `docs/ddflow/research/requirements-management.md` and merged it (commits 6a916e730, 31c2fd758, 965cb7e7c).
- Task `RQM-research` completed through its gates, which ran in this order:
  - rules and implement: passed.
  - standards: passed, but the review was of the first commit. One medium finding (event log not committed with the doc) was fixed afterwards and not re-reviewed.
  - dedupe: skipped, with a reason on record.
- I recorded 10 research notes: `R-req-kind-inert`, `-checks-unwired`, `-no-mcp-client`, `-no-layers-no-remote`, `-rules-cut`, `-inject-timeline`, `-capability-gaps`, `-planned-coverage`, `-design` and `-other-tools`. The last two are THEORETICAL; the other eight are CONFIRMED.
- I re-checked the sub-agents' headline claims against the code or by running the commands. Those include no callers for checks and waivers, no MCP client calls, no `services/org`, the brief cutting every rule, and the 1-of-57 claim block.
- The event log is committed on main (my shard `.ddflow/events/res-requirements.jsonl` plus its 4 blobs).

## Do requirements exist or are they planned?
**A `requirement` record kind already exists, but it is inert.**
- `ddflow/templates/kinds/requirement.toml` defines the fields and a lifecycle (proposed, approved, implemented, verified). `ddflow record requirement list` works.
- It has no scope, no strength, no verify command and no layer or owner.
- Nothing delivers it to a session. `RecordKind.applies` is declared but nothing reads it, and `inject.collect` (`services/guidance/inject.py:104`) returns only rules and decisions.

**Product requirements are planned, engineering requirements are not.**
- `P-product-docs` covers product requirements (`PD-req-kind`, `PD-lint`, `PD-trace`).
- I read 154 open non-RQM tasks (2,121 of 2,670 tasks in total); none plans "CMake >= 3.25 / Conan / no in-source builds" as a scoped, injected, verified record.
- The pieces it would reuse are planned across other phases: `P-goals`, `P-record-contract`, `B-pipe-*`, `P-org-config`, `P-safeguards`, `OB-rules-glob`, `KB-*`.

## Capability matrix (condensed)
Y = present, N = absent, P = partial. The full 14-column matrix with file:line evidence is in section 2 of the doc.

| Kind | edit | remove | supersede | dupe/conflict check | glob scope | re-injection | enforcement | external source | MCP |

| rules | Y | Y (retire) | **N** | Y | Y | P (claim, brief, gate, review; cut in practice) | P (ranking only) | N | Y |
| decisions | **N** | **N** | Y | Y (plus unreconciled pairs) | Y | same doors | P (warn) | N | Y |
| lessons | **N** | **N** | P | Y | P | brief only | P (`lesson verify`) | N | Y; no show |
| memory | P | Y (forget) | N | Y | N | brief only | N | N | Y |
| requirement kind | Y | Y | Y | Y (add-time) | **N** | **N** | **N** | N | only via `record` |
| doc types | hand edit | hand edit | `extends` only | N | Y | via B-dt-rules guidance | P (`docs check`) | local only | `docs check` only |
| skills | N | N | N | N | BM25 rank | one brief line each | N | N | via brief |
| subagent definitions | N | N | N | N | N | launch brief only | N | N | via brief |
| harness instruction files | refresh | N | digest stamp | N | none | once | pre-commit drift | N | `setup` |
| companions / standards gate | N | N | N | N | gate list | none | recorded `unavailable` | **never called by ddflow** | Y |
| goals, principles, policies | planned (`B-goal-*`, `B-org-policy`) | | | | | | `[enforce]` knobs only | | |

- **Checks and waivers:** `services/guidance/checks.py` and `waivers.py` are built and tested, but no code outside `services/guidance` calls them and no check kind is registered.
- **Reminder footer:** the cadenced footer (every 12 calls and 240 s) names undone obligations only, never rule text.

## Gaps, ranked
1. **Rules never reach a fresh session.**
   - `ddflow brief` prints "7 more cut to fit session.brief_max_tokens", so none of the 7 rules is delivered.
   - The claim block for `B-dt-rules` shows 1 of 57 applying records, a warn-level decision (`D-acp-r2`).
   - The cause is that ranking puts block above warn above advisory, all 7 rules are advisory, the repo has 263 decisions, and no rule is pinned.
   - The subagent launch brief carries no rules either.
2. **The requirement kind is inert.** No scope, strength or verify, no provider seam into the guidance engine, and `inject.collect` is closed.
3. **No compliance check.** The checks and waivers engine has no caller.
4. **No periodic re-instruction.**
   - The UserPromptSubmit hook injects 0 bytes.
   - PreCompact cannot inject; PostCompact, Stop and PostToolUse have no handler; there is no `SubagentStart` handler.
5. **No delivery or application evidence.** A read-receipt for text injected into a model is impossible; the design uses delivered, applied and checked as three proofs instead.
6. **No external source and no MCP client.**
   - ddflow is only an MCP server; its one client call sends `initialize` and nothing else.
   - codeguide enters the standards gate as one sentence of prose for the agent (`mcp_instructions.md:158`).
7. **No org or team layer**, and no `[org]`, `[policy]` or `[guidance]` config section.
8. **Conflict detection** exists only between decisions.
9. **Instruction-file output** is limited: no `GEMINI.md`, no `copilot-instructions.md`, no `.github/instructions`, no `.claude/rules`.
10. **Smaller gaps:** rule supersede, doc-type list/show, positional doc-type rule ids, traceability, and mid-session changes (ddflow advertises `listChanged:false`).

## Recommended design
- **Data model.** Extend the shipped `requirement` kind rather than adding a second one. New fields: `class` (product, constraint, standard, policy), `strength` (must, should, may), `globs`, `contexts` (named matchers such as cmake, conan, cpp), `topic` and `expect` (conflict key), `verify` (command, pattern, file, config, reviewer or mcp), `source` (layer, uri, rev, digest), plus owner, version and supersedes. `PD-req-kind` adds its EARS and baseline fields to the same descriptor.
- **Layering.** org enforced > org defaults > team > project > local > task. A lower layer may only tighten, unless a person records a scoped, reasoned, expiring waiver. Remote records arrive as `trust=imported`. They are pinned by digest, use ETag and keep the last good copy, and can only propose, never apply a MUST. A conflict sets `contested`, which already keeps a record out of injection.
- **Injection tiers.**
  - Charter: one line per MUST, 250 tokens, never trimmed, replacing the "N more cut" line.
  - Contextual: by glob or context at claim, pre-edit, gate and review.
  - On demand: search.
  - Digest: a reminder on a cadence, reset on compaction.
  - Change: BINDING changes via `B-rc-changes`.
- **Compliance.**
  - `ddflow requirement check` records evidence; a check that cannot run is `unavailable`, never passed.
  - A `requirements` gate is added through `pipeline.require` when a MUST matches the item's scope.
  - The agent reports `applied`, `not_applicable` or `violated` per MUST, and a mismatch with the mechanical result is flagged.

chunk_findings.detail: The end-to-end regression test records `implement` as `passed` for a docs-only task, so it does not exercise the reported failure mode: the bug is that `implement` is a required gate and a `skip` does not satisfy it. An incomplete fix that still requires `implement` (while only removing/changing `unit_tests`) would pass this test, because the scenario here never skips or omits `implement`. The test also records `rules`, `standards`, and `dedupe`, while the change describes the new doc pipeline as `research, docs, merge`; against that intended pipeline `gate record D1 implement --outcome passed` should be rejected.

chunk_findings.detail: [D-doc-pipeline-from-globs] says the doc pipeline is derived from declared globs and only verified against the actual diff, so a task declared as docs-only that later changes a code path should still run the doc pipeline and then be rejected at completion when that path escapes the doc globs. The new docstring says “The diff decides, never the declared globs”, which implements the opposite policy. Given a task whose declared globs are all documentation but whose actual diff includes `src/main.py`, this change would classify it as a non-doc task and run the normal code pipeline; if `implement` and `unit_tests` pass, the undeclared code change can merge instead of being caught by the doc-pipeline completion check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/gates.py:39 (doc_globs docstring)

chunk_findings.detail: [D-doc-pipeline-from-globs] The new `diff_is_docs_only` derives doc-only status solely from the actual changed `paths` and never consults `item.globs`, contrary to the decision that the doc pipeline is derived from the declared globs and then verified against the actual diff. Input: `item.kind == "task"`, `item.promote_to is None`, declared globs `["src/**", "docs/**"]`, and actual diff paths `["docs/notes.md"]`. The function returns `True`, so `outcomes.py` switches gates to `kind_pipeline(cfg, "doc")` and the normal code gates are skipped even though the task’s declared globs are not all documentation.

chunk_findings.detail: In `test_an_excused_required_gate_is_not_ahead`, changing the worktree change from `docs/x.md` to `lib/x.py` makes `unit_tests` a required, unsatisfied gate for a code diff. The test never skips or passes `unit_tests`, so `_ahead` will include `"unit_tests"`, and the assertion at line 24 (`assert "unit_tests" not in ahead, ahead`) will fail. The original `docs/x.md` change was the thing that excused `unit_tests`; replacing it with `lib/x.py` removes the excuse and makes the test fail in the normal test run.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ahead_of_diff.py:21

chunk_findings.detail: The new tests encode that the actual diff, not the declared globs, selects the doc pipeline: `test_a_diff_of_documents_only_is_docs_only` asserts `diff_is_docs_only(_task("src/**"), cfg, ["docs/a.md", "README.md", "docs/x/y.md"])` is true, and `test_declared_doc_globs_alone_keep_the_task_pipeline` asserts a task whose declared globs are all docs but whose actual change is code gets `unit_tests`. This contradicts [D-doc-pipeline-from-globs], which states the doc pipeline is derived from declared globs and that a task whose declared globs are all documentation runs the doc pipeline, with completion only verifying the actual diff stays inside those doc globs. A task declaring `src/**` is not doc-only under that decision, so these assertions would force the implementation to misclassify tasks.

Because of this, the test would still pass on a broken fix that removes `unit_tests` and reviewer independence but leaves `implement` in the doc pipeline; a docs-only change with no implementation would still be unable to complete without `--force`. The triage says “implement is attainable on a docs task,” but that is exactly the wrong gate for a docs-only task and does not address the finding.

chunk_findings.detail: The documented gate selection rule is inverted relative to the decision. The new knob text says the doc pipeline is chosen from “ACTUAL changed paths” and “The diff decides, never the declared globs,” but D-doc-pipeline-from-globs requires the doc pipeline to be derived from the task’s declared globs, with the actual diff checked only at completion. A task created with globs=["docs/**"] before any diff exists would, under this documented behavior, be put in the task pipeline rather than the doc pipeline, so implement/unit_tests remain required and completion still fails without --force — the exact bug this change is meant to fix.
chunk_findings.title: [D-doc-pipeline-from-globs] ddflow/config_sections/gates.py:39

chunk_findings.detail: The new `diff_is_docs_only` function derives the doc pipeline solely from the actual changed paths and explicitly says “The ACTUAL diff decides, never the declared globs,” which is the opposite of [D-doc-pipeline-from-globs]. That decision requires the doc pipeline to be derived from the task’s declared globs and only verified against the actual diff. Concrete failure: a task with declared globs `["src/**", "docs/**"]` and an actual diff containing only `docs/foo.md` is classified as docs-only and routed to the doc pipeline, even though its declared globs are not all documentation. Conversely, a task with declared globs `["docs/**"]` and an actual diff containing `src/main.py` is classified as not docs-only and routed to the normal task pipeline, so the required verification that the actual diff stays inside the doc globs is never performed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/kinds.py:27 diff_is_docs_only

chunk_findings.detail: The change from `docs/x.md` to `lib/x.py` removes the docs-only precondition of `test_an_excused_required_gate_is_not_ahead`. A code change under `lib/` leaves `unit_tests` required, so `_ahead(...)` will include `"unit_tests"`, and the next line’s `assert "unit_tests" not in ahead` fails. This test is now a regression against the fix rather than a passing regression test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ahead_of_diff.py:21

chunk_findings.detail: `test_block_policy_does_not_refuse_on_an_excused_gate` has the same defect. With `lib/x.py`, `unit_tests` is a required later gate and is not in the skip loop `("research", "rules", "implement", "rubber_duck", "critic", "standards")`. Under `gates.enforce_order=block`, the CLI will refuse one of those `gate skip` commands, so the loop’s `assert code == 0, out + err` fails. The test needs a docs-only change to keep `unit_tests` excused.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ahead_of_diff.py:31

chunk_findings.detail: The summary and the five-rung rule contradict each other. Line 14 says an upgrade is soft only when the digest is unchanged, the client honours `list_changed`, or facade mode is on, so an additive change for a client that ignores `list_changed` and is not in facade mode would be hard. Line 18, rung 3, says additive changes are soft for every client. An implementer following the summary would emit a hard upgrade for that client even though the actual rule says soft.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/mcp-soft-upgrade.md:14

chunk_findings.detail: The new tests encode that the actual diff alone decides the pipeline, ignoring declared globs: `diff_is_docs_only(_task("src/**"), cfg, ["docs/a.md", "README.md", "docs/x/y.md"])` is asserted true, while `diff_is_docs_only(_task("docs/**"), cfg, ["docs/a.md", "ddflow/api/review.py"])` is asserted false. This directly contradicts [D-doc-pipeline-from-globs], which says the doc pipeline is derived from declared globs and verified against the actual diff: a task whose declared globs are all documentation runs the doc pipeline, and completion verifies the actual diff stays inside the doc globs. Under that decision, `_task("docs/**")` with a code path in the diff should still select the doc pipeline and then fail completion because the diff strays outside the doc globs; the test instead keeps it on the task pipeline.

data.body:
Operator 2026-10-21 (verbatim): "Check this tool - https://www.accrete.ai/why-accrete and research it and see if there are ideas we can pick up for ddflow to implement, as well as separately, would ddflow be easy to integrate with accrete and give me opinion, phase + tasks for the gaps, with proper dependencies and wave to implement"

Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/accrete.md (task ACF-research) and research notes R-accrete-*.

VERDICT IN ONE PARAGRAPH: Accrete (accrete.ai) is a closed, sales-led enterprise 'context graph / Knowledge Engine' vendor (plus a US-government product, Argus). It publishes NO public API, SDK, MCP spec or webhook docs (REPORTED by a third-party catalog and confirmed by the absence on every page read), so an Accrete-specific adapter cannot be specified or tested today. Almost every idea it sells (decision rationale, provenance, confidence, temporal validity, permissioned knowledge, memory consolidation, citations) is already planned in ddflow (P-lessons, P-decisions, P-agent-memory, P-knowledge-hub, P-requirements, P-observe) and D-graph-scope-r1 explicitly declines a knowledge-graph memory. This phase therefore adds ONLY the gaps: a read-only 'why corpus' export an external consumer can ingest, an egress-checked consult of an external knowledge source, a recall probe built from the project's own history, and propose-only memory consolidation, plus decision, vendor verification, end-to-end and docs tasks. No Accrete-specific code is built until Accrete gives access (ACF-verify) and the operator says so (ACF-decide).

WAVES: W1 ACF-research -> ACF-decide. W2 (parallel, disjoint globs) ACF-why-export, ACF-consult-out, ACF-recall-probe, ACF-memory-consolidate, ACF-verify. W3 ACF-e2e. W4 ACF-docs. Held behind the P-gaps core/docs wave per D-old-work-behind-core-docs (phase needs).

LINKED, NOT RE-ADDED (already planned): decision traces/ruled-out log = D-reasoning-log + B-am-capture + B-dec-model; per-record provenance/validity/confidence = KB-envelope, KB-attest, B-security-provenance; permissioning = KB-scope, KB-auth, SE-sensitivity; outcome feedback = P-lessons.recurrence, P-lessons.effect, P-observe.effect; staleness = PL-staleness, B-dec-review; citations = RQM-reviewer, RQM-ack; inbound remote knowledge/MCP = RQM-sources, RQM-mcp-client, KB-mirror; ddflow as MCP server for another agent platform = P-control-planes (MCP profiles, scoped tokens), P-remote.serve; outbound notification webhooks = CP-notify-sinks; platform tool guard = PM-descriptor, PM-guard.
data.title: Accrete fit: ideas from a context-graph/knowledge-engine vendor and the generic seams (why-corpus export, egress-checked consult, recall probe, memory consolidation) that make any such service easy to connect

data.body: Write docs/ddflow/research/accrete.md from the research notes R-accrete-*: claims tagged VERIFIED/REPORTED/UNKNOWN, ranked ideas with ddflow counterpart ids, integration analysis (ddflow as client, ddflow as source), the honest opinion. Python blocks formatted with ruff format.
data.title: Research doc: what Accrete is (evidence-tagged), ideas to adopt ranked, integration fit in both directions

data.body: Ask the operator and file docs/ddflow/decisions/accrete-fit.md; record decisions with --globs. Recommended defaults from the research doc: (1) NO Accrete-specific adapter now: it has no public API/SDK/MCP docs; build the generic seams only and revisit when ACF-verify has facts. (2) ddflow as SOURCE first (read-only 'why corpus' export, ACF-why-export): cheapest, no inbound trust problem; ddflow as CLIENT second (ACF-consult-out) and only through RQM-mcp-client. (3) Anything leaving the machine goes through an egress door with the sensitivity ceiling, a preview and a confirm (knob: [consult_out].confirm, default true; never auto for agent-origin text), and is recorded with a digest. (4) Answers from an external service are trust=imported, fenced, never an instruction and never a gate pass; an unreachable service is unavailable, never passed. (5) Keep D-graph-scope-r1: no knowledge-graph memory is built; the export carries edges, it does not become a graph store. (6) Which of ACF-recall-probe and ACF-memory-consolidate to build (both are useful without Accrete).
data.title: Operator decisions: build generic seams only (no Accrete adapter until access), what may leave the machine, which of W2 to build

data.body: One more export kind on the existing registry (services/export, P-extension-seams.registry): each line is a record with id, kind, text, trust and origin, validity (status, superseded_by), governs (globs), alternatives rejected, evidence ids, and a content digest (KB-envelope). Read-only; no secrets (redact), records above the sensitivity ceiling are withheld through the new egress door (SX-egress-door), the manifest lists what was withheld and why. `--dry-run` previews. Any consumer (an Accrete ingestion job, a RAG pipeline, another agent) can use it; nothing Accrete-specific. Tests: supersede edge present, sensitive record withheld, deterministic output, imported-trust records marked so a consumer does not re-export them as operator words.
data.title: Export kind `why`: decisions, rejected alternatives, lessons, research verdicts as an open JSONL corpus with provenance, validity and supersede/governs edges

data.body: The gap RQM-mcp-client does not cover: the INBOUND read of standards exists there; sending a QUERY that contains project text out does not. Build [consult_out.<name>] (server = an MCP companion id or URL, tool, allowed_fields, sensitivity ceiling, confirm default true, timeout, daily call cap = cost knob; auth only by environment variable NAME, never a value in config). Flow: build the query from allowed fields only, run egress and record-hazard scan, show the exact payload, require a confirm (an agent cannot confirm its own consult), call through the RQM-mcp-client transport, record `consult.sent` (digest, destination, byte count) and the answer as trust=imported fenced text with a source. Failure, timeout or an auth error records the consult `unavailable`; it never satisfies a gate and never falls back silently. Tests with a stub server: payload excludes labelled records, no confirm = no call, timeout = unavailable, answer is fenced and not an instruction, call cap enforced.
data.title: Egress-checked consult: ask an external knowledge service a question built from cleared fields, preview and confirm first, answer stored as fenced trust=imported

data.body: Accrete markets a tacit-knowledge coverage score (vendor-reported, unverified). The idea worth taking: measure whether ddflow's own memory surfaces the right prior reasoning. Build `ddflow recall-probe`: derive probe questions from fixed bugs and superseded decisions (question = the situation, expected = the lesson/decision id that governs it), withhold the answer record from the query text, run brief/recall/search, report hit@k per surface and a list of misses (candidate lessons that should exist or be scoped). Deterministic, no LLM required; uses the evalkit and B-am-eval fixtures; output is a metric, never a gate. Related not duplicate: P-lessons.effect (repeat rate of recorded lessons) and B-am-eval (seeded fixtures).
data.title: Recall probe from the project's own history: held-out 'why' facts (decision rationale, bug root causes) scored against brief, recall and search

data.body: P-lessons.curate dedupes and merges LESSONS; nothing turns the many small operational memories and session notes into a reusable judgment (Accrete's 'memory consolidation'). Cluster memories with services/similar.py, draft one lesson or rule candidate per cluster with the source ids as citations, file it as a proposal (trust=agent, never active), and mark the sources 'consolidated-into' only after a person accepts. Idempotent; budget knob; no network. Tests: cluster threshold, proposal never active, sources untouched until acceptance, re-run adds nothing.
data.title: Propose-only consolidation of operational memories into lessons or rules (cluster, distil, cite sources); a person accepts

data.body: BLOCKED ON THE OPERATOR/ACCRETE: needs a demo or trial. Questions to put to Accrete, each answer recorded as a research note with a probe: (1) is there a documented API/SDK/OpenAPI, an MCP server or client, webhooks; (2) auth (OAuth/Okta/API key), per-tenant and per-user permission model, audit log; (3) can a customer-built MCP server (their 'forward-deployed engineering with MCP servers') expose ddflow's read-only tools; (4) ingestion formats for structured decision records; (5) deployment (SaaS, VPC, on-prem, classified), data residency, retention, training-on-customer-data policy; (6) pricing basis and rate limits; (7) what the 2-4 week 'knowledge map' needs from us. Replace every UNKNOWN in the research doc table that gets an answer; if the answers are no/none, mark the phase's integration tasks not applicable instead of building them.
data.title: Verify Accrete's real interfaces once access exists (API, MCP servers, auth, tenancy, data residency); operator-blocked, record research notes

data.body: A stub service (stdio MCP and HTTP) stands in for any context-graph vendor. Scenarios: (a) the export ingests into the stub and a superseded decision stays superseded; (b) a labelled record is absent from export and from a consult payload; (c) consult without confirm sends nothing; (d) the stub down, slow, 401 and returning an injection string: unavailable recorded, never a gate pass, answer fenced as imported; (e) recall-probe misses become lesson candidates and consolidation proposals stay inactive until accepted; (f) a custom companion entry for the stub (companions.toml overlay) is registered and its gate coverage shown. Run with pytest -n 48.
data.title: End-to-end with a fake knowledge service: export the why corpus, consult out with confirm, failures are unavailable, nothing leaks

data.body: One operator guide: what leaves the machine and how it is previewed and confirmed, how to point any vendor at the read-only MCP profile or the why export, how to add a custom companion, what 'unavailable' means for a consult, the recall probe and consolidation commands, and a short Accrete section pointing at docs/ddflow/research/accrete.md. Docs check passes; python blocks formatted with ruff format.
data.title: Document connecting an external knowledge service: the why export, consult-out knobs, egress rules, the Accrete verdict

Every other gate is recorded, and the merge landed as `b351d8f60`. My event log is committed as `61e1b6ec4`, and no push was done.

## What Accrete is

- **Product (VERIFIED):** a closed, sales-led "context layer / Knowledge Engine Platform" for enterprises. It also sells Argus to US government.
- **Claimed architecture (VERIFIED as claims only):** a graph with provenance, confidence and temporal validity per edge, built from decision traces. Memory is consolidated and answers carry citations. Agents are orchestrated, with multi-tenant permissioning (Okta and RBAC).
- **Trust page:** it lists SOC 2 Type 1 and 2, CMMC, DoD IL4/IL5, HIPAA and ITAR. Argus is "built to the FedRAMP High standard"; no authorisation is stated.
- **Interfaces:** I found no public API, SDK, OpenAPI, webhook or MCP documentation. The only mention is one blog sentence about a "forward-deployed engineering model with MCP servers", with no endpoints or schemas. A third-party catalog agrees (REPORTED).
- **Benchmarks:** 58% lower token cost, 19 of 34 tacit facts versus 1 for RAG, 92% time saving and so on are vendor numbers with no method (REPORTED, note verdict THEORETICAL).
- **Pricing:** demo only, so unknown.

## Ranked ideas

Almost everything Accrete sells is already planned in ddflow. `D-graph-scope-r1` also declines a knowledge-graph memory, so I did not propose one.

1. **Recall probe built from the project's own history (new).** `ACF-recall-probe` scores whether brief, recall and search surface the right prior reasoning for fixed bugs and superseded decisions. Small effort, high value, low risk. Related to `B-am-eval` and `P-lessons.effect`.
2. **"Why" corpus export (new).** `ACF-why-export` is a read-only JSONL export of decisions, lessons and research with supersede and governs edges, filtered by the sensitivity egress door. Small effort, high value, low risk.
3. **Memory consolidation (new).** `ACF-memory-consolidate` is propose-only. It clusters operational memories into lesson or rule candidates with citations, and a person accepts. Small effort, medium value, low risk.
4. **Already planned, linked rather than re-added:**
   - Decision traces: `D-reasoning-log`, `B-am-capture`, `B-dec-model`.
   - Provenance and validity: `KB-envelope`, `KB-attest`.
   - Permissioning: `KB-scope`, `KB-auth`, `SE-sensitivity`.
   - Outcome feedback and staleness: `P-lessons.recurrence`, `P-lessons.effect`, `PL-staleness`, `P-observe.effect`.
   - Citations: `RQM-reviewer`, `RQM-ack`.

## Integration verdict

My opinion: do not build an Accrete adapter now. There is no public interface to specify or test against, the sales cycle is demo-gated, and the benchmarks are unverified. ddflow already covers most of the value locally, and sending project text to a third party is a publication decision for the operator.

- **ddflow as a client of Accrete:** hard today because the interface is unknown. Once `RQM-mcp-client` and `RQM-sources` exist, a read of an Accrete MCP server is moderate, about 3 to 5 days. Answers would be trust=imported and fenced, with unreachable recorded as unavailable and never passed.
  - Accrete as a reviewer is not recommended: its model family and output are unknown.
  - ddflow has no MCP client or outbound query path today, which I confirmed in the code.
- **Accrete as a consumer of ddflow:** easy for reading once the export exists, because ddflow already has an MCP server, an event log and export kinds. Whether Accrete can ingest it is unknown. Accrete agents claiming work from the ddflow queue is hard and not advisable.
- **What would make it easy:** Accrete publishing an OpenAPI spec or a documented MCP server, per-tenant tokens, and a structured-record ingest.

## Phase `P-accrete-fit`

The phase needs the hold ids behind the core and docs wave: `B-gap-log-scale`, `B-gap-lanes`, `B-gap-plan-lint`, `P-doc-templates`, `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`. I checked the graph over the folded state: no cycles, and every need exists.

| 3 | `ACF-e2e` | the four wave-2 build tasks |
| 4 | `ACF-docs` | `ACF-e2e` |

`ACF-consult-out` is the outbound query with an egress check, preview and person-confirm before anything leaves the machine. `ACF-verify` is operator-blocked: it needs a demo or trial, and it carries the questions to put to Accrete. `ACF-e2e` runs against a fake knowledge service, so it does not wait on `ACF-verify`. `ACF-decide` carries the recommended defaults. **What Pi is**
- **Identity (VERIFIED, I read the docs and source):** Pi (pi.dev) is a minimal terminal coding-agent harness from Earendil Inc. The repo is `github.com/earendil-works/pi`, MIT licence, `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.3.0, read at commit `cae9fd2`.
- **What it leaves out (VERIFIED):** it ships no sub-agents, plan mode, permission prompts or todos, so the user adds those as extensions.
- **Interfaces (VERIFIED):** TUI, print, `--mode json`, `--mode rpc` and a TypeScript SDK. It reads `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, and skills from `.pi/skills` and `.agents/skills`.
- **Extensions (VERIFIED):** TypeScript, run inside the Pi process. They can use:
  - `tool_call`, which can block a call;
  - `session_before_compact`;
  - `agent_before_settle`, which can request one more continuation;
  - `session_start`, `input` and `session_shutdown`.
- **Built-in MCP client (VERIFIED):** it supports stdio and streamable HTTP, protocol 2025-11-25, with `clientInfo` name `pi`. It re-lists tools on `tools/list_changed` (`runtime.ts:380`). I found no handler for prompts or resources changes.
- **Sessions (VERIFIED):** JSONL trees with branching and compaction.
- **Security model (VERIFIED):** Pi asks for no approval before tool calls, so containment has to come from ddflow or the OS.
- **Claims I could not check (REPORTED):** the "hundreds of thousands of weekly users" figure, the Pi 1.0 release date, and the community ACP adapters (`pi-acp` and forks) that wrap the RPC mode.
- **Nothing was run.** I only read docs and source and executed no Pi code, so `R-pidev-lane-rpc` is THEORETICAL.

**Overlap**
- **Verdict:** Pi is the agent; ddflow is the queue, lease, gate and record layer around any agent. Pi has none of ddflow's features, and ddflow has no model loop or session tree.
- **Already in the repo:** `P-agent-parity.new-descriptors` lists `pi`, and `P-agent-parity.continuation` mentions Pi's plugin hooks. There was no `pi.toml`, fixture or delta note.
- **Instruction files:** `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` already work with Pi with no change.

**Traps for a Pi integration (VERIFIED in the docs)**
1. Pi MCP servers default to `codemode` exposure, so the model does not see ddflow's tools unless the entry says `exposure: direct` or sets `toolExposure`.
2. In print, JSON and RPC modes, `.pi/extensions` and `.pi/mcp.json` are skipped unless the project is trusted or `--approve` is passed, and no error is shown. A headless lane would run without ddflow.
3. `pi.exec` has no stdin option, so the hook extension has to use `node:child_process` to pipe the payload to `ddflow hooks run`.
4. Pi sends anonymous install telemetry by default (`enableInstallTelemetry`).

**Ranked ideas (full table with effort, value and risk is in the doc)**
1. Write the client's own tool tiers (`exposure`) from ddflow's tool profiles and add a doctor check that the model can see ddflow. New: `PI-exposure-map`.
2. Make verify detect silent client-side skips such as the trust gate and report `unavailable`, not done. New: `PI-onboard-verify`.

4. Decide whether gate hooks fail closed, as Pi's `tool_call` does, or open. This goes into `PI-decide`.
5. Use a session-entry id as an incremental cursor for transcript import. New: `PI-session-ingest`.

- **ddflow supports Pi as a harness: moderate.** The descriptor and MCP entry are easy. The moderate part is a new hook dialect plus a TypeScript extension that `adopt` would install. Enforcement exists only while the extension is loaded and trusted.
- **ddflow drives Pi as a lane worker: easy to moderate.** `pi --mode rpc` is a documented JSONL protocol with prompt, steer, follow-up and abort, and `agent_settled` marks completion. It needs `--approve` and a lane-private agent directory. ACP is only a fallback.
- **Pi consuming ddflow's records: easy, nothing new.** Reading Pi's sessions back is the only addition (`PI-session-ingest`).
- **Opinion:** support it, at a low tier (fixtures first), and record every "could not run" as `unavailable`. Reasons against:

data.body: Research R-wait-wake (CONFIRMED): ddflow has no notification path; a blocked agent learns of a release only by re-asking. Observed 2026-10-21: fx-version-skew ended its turn with three items blocked on other agents' leases and nothing resumed it; the lead had to run a background ddflow wait and message it. Design: (1) the agent contract in the launch brief and MCP instructions: while waiting on a lease, block in 'ddflow wait --item X --globs ...' in a loop (each call up to the tool timeout) instead of ending the turn; (2) on lease release/merge/complete ddflow emits a 'lease.released' wake to every registered waiter (the existing 'woke' list in complete output); (3) a waiter registry maps waiter -> how to reach it (a harness session id for 'send_message', an inbound watch URL, or a polling 'ddflow wait'), and 'ddflow wait --notify' registers it; (4) an orchestrator-side helper that resumes finished subagents (SendMessage) when their wake fires. Reuse the approvals/ask engine and the existing waiting.py register.
data.title: A waiting agent is woken when the lease it waits on is released (and never ends its turn while waiting)

data.body: Observed: globs declared at claim (ddflow/services/gates/**, tests/golden/**) overlap by PREFIX (L-glob-prefix-overlap), hold files nobody touches, and block parallel agents for hours; agents then pile up uncommitted work. Design: claim records intent globs as advisory; the pre-commit/pre-edit hook acquires a lease on the EXACT files being changed when they are free (and queues/waits with the holder named when not); files are released when merged or idle. Keep [lease].shared_globs (generated/pinned outputs) and new_file_globs exempt. A knob chooses declared (today) vs lazy.
data.title: Leases on demand: the commit/edit hook takes an exact-file lease at first write when the file is free; declared globs are advisory

data.body: globs_overlap is prefix-based by design (L-glob-prefix-overlap, L-wildcard-globs-scheduler-overlap): 'a/**' overlaps 'a/x.py' though the holder never touches x.py. Compute overlap from the holder's actual changed files (git diff of its worktree against base plus its literal declared paths) so disjoint files under one directory run in parallel; fall back to the prefix rule only when the holder has no worktree.
data.title: Lease overlap is judged on the files a holder actually changed, not on glob prefixes

data.body: Each agent works in its own worktree, so an exclusive per-file lease mostly guards merge conflicts git can already resolve. Use 'git merge-tree' to test whether the two branches' changes to a file merge cleanly; allow concurrent edits then, and make the second merge rebase (re-run the pin regeneration) instead of waiting. Exclusive leases stay for generated/pinned files and for real conflicts.
data.title: Optimistic concurrency: two agents may change disjoint hunks of one file; the lease only orders the merge

data.body: fx-Ba2df74d558 held ddflow/infra/log.py, tests/golden/** and ddflow/core/redact* for hours, blocking three other agents, while it only waited on CI. Release files no longer changed (hand back on 'ddflow update --globs'), auto-release after a merge of those files, and show 'held for N hours, last write M minutes ago' in the refusal.
data.title: Release a file's lease when its change is merged or the agent is idle, not at item completion
